cim: Chinese Agricultural AI Innovation Lags Behind Production and Consumption Efficiency
cim_eredeti: Chinese Agricultural AI Innovation Lags Behind Production and Consumption Efficiency
szoveg_eredeti:
Chinese Agricultural AI Innovation Lags Behind Production and Consumption Efficiency

Across 30 provincial-level regions in China evaluated between 2019 and 2024, the primary systemic bottleneck in converting technological advances into sustainable agri-food outcomes occurred at the initial research and innovation stage rather than in farming production or consumer food supply. An empirical study published in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems constructed a dynamic three-stage network directional distance function data envelopment analysis model to evaluate overall and stage-specific efficiencies across agricultural artificial intelligence technological innovation, sustainable agricultural production, and sustainable agricultural consumption. The research revealed that while the national mean overall efficiency reached 0.7284, the first stage dedicated to developing agricultural artificial intelligence technologies lagged severely with a mean score of 0.4177, compared to 0.9053 for sustainable agricultural production and 0.8880 for sustainable agricultural consumption.

The analytical framework was designed to address a critical black-box limitation in conventional single-stage data envelopment analysis models, which typically measure initial inputs against final outputs without uncovering intermediate operational breakdowns. The authors, Shuya Yan, Guotao Yang, and Xiaoran Li, structured the multi-stage conversion process to trace sequential resource flows across the agri-food network. Rather than measuring the subjective preferences of individual consumers or the farm-level adoption rates of specific automated tools, the model quantified provincial-level macro efficiency. Intermediate link variables connected contiguous stages, while intertemporal carry-over variables captured persistent agricultural fixed-asset capital formation, providing a quantitative mechanism to evaluate how research investments transform into production capabilities and ultimately satisfy nutritional needs with minimized waste under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 12 framework.

To evaluate the first stage of agricultural artificial intelligence innovation, the researchers measured regional research and development expenditures and research personnel as inputs against the number of granted agricultural artificial intelligence invention patents categorized under IPC classification A01 as the stage output. Because provincial-level statistics dedicated exclusively to agricultural technological research are not published directly, expenditures and staffing were estimated using national agricultural research shares and the proportional weight of agricultural value added in provincial gross domestic product. By utilizing granted patents rather than raw patent applications, the model evaluated innovative outputs that successfully passed formal substantive examination. The empirical findings demonstrated that no province achieved frontier status in this first stage, with 26 of the 30 sampled regions exhibiting major efficiency bottlenecks and 17 categorized under the highest warning priority level.

The second stage of the network model tracked the conversion of granted artificial intelligence patents alongside conventional inputs—specifically cultivated land area and government expenditures on agriculture, forestry, and water conservancy—into sustainable farming outcomes. Ecological integrity was captured through provincial species richness as a desirable output, while intermediate linkages transferred into the third stage comprised food supply capacity, rural per capita disposable income as an index of food affordability, and total grain output. Food supply capacity was constructed via the global entropy-weighting method by evaluating standardized labor productivity across agriculture, livestock farming, and fisheries over the six-year observation period. Thirteen provincial jurisdictions operated directly on the efficiency frontier for this production stage, although major production-stage bottlenecks remained concentrated in specific regions including Hubei, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hunan, and Hebei.

The final stage evaluated sustainable agricultural consumption by absorbing intermediate outputs from production alongside external food inputs measured through the economic value of agricultural product imports. Desirable output was measured through per capita grain consumption, while per capita grain waste served as an undesirable output subjected to directional contraction constraints. Because direct continuous provincial measurements of food waste are unavailable, waste volumes were estimated from total grain output, resident population records, and published consumption-stage waste coefficients from urban catering and nutritional reports, intentionally excluding pre-consumption losses occurring in transit, storage, and processing. Six provinces attained the efficiency frontier in this consumption conversion stage, whereas eight jurisdictions recorded efficiency scores below 0.8000, signaling deficiencies in converting local food supplies and imports into effective human consumption without generating excessive waste.

Temporal analysis indicated that national overall efficiency followed a fluctuating upward trajectory over the six-year panel, declining slightly from 0.7125 in 2019 to 0.7007 in 2020 before climbing to 0.7473 in 2024, representing an overall gain of 4.89 percent. Overall efficiency increased across 19 provinces, accounting for 63.33 percent of the examined jurisdictions. At the regional level, the eastern region ranked highest with a six-year mean overall efficiency of 0.7605 and an expansion of 9.56 percent over time. The western region followed with an overall mean of 0.7353 but registered only marginal growth of 0.66 percent, while the central region recorded the lowest mean efficiency at 0.6749 despite experiencing an increase of 4.16 percent. Individual provincial scores varied widely: Qinghai, Beijing, and Shanghai achieved top mean scores of 0.9936, 0.9742, and 0.9555, respectively, whereas Hebei, Hunan, and Jiangxi exhibited the lowest overall efficiencies at 0.3997, 0.4496, and 0.5431.

The structural nature of geographical disparities was examined using Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition and non-parametric Gaussian kernel density estimation. The mean overall Dagum Gini coefficient across the 2019 to 2024 period was 0.1097, peaking at 0.1167 in 2021 before moderating to 0.1068 by 2024. Inequality decomposition revealed that transvariation density—representing the mathematical overlap between regional efficiency distributions—served as the dominant contributor to overall disparity, accounting for an average share of 46.56 percent. Within-region disparities accounted for 31.42 percent, while net between-region inequality contributed 22.02 percent. Kernel density curves showed persistent multimodality and prolonged distribution tails across all years, demonstrating that provincial efficiency did not converge toward a single concentrated distribution, with the central region exhibiting particularly prominent internal polarization.

Sensitivity and robustness checks across five methodological variations confirmed the stability of the baseline efficiency rankings. Re-estimating the models after independently deleting agricultural research spending and personnel yielded mean overall efficiencies of 0.7148 and 0.7249, respectively, retaining Spearman rank correlation coefficients above 0.9880 with the baseline model. Modifying the moving-window duration from three years to two and four periods produced average rank changes of only 0.67 positions, while excluding the four direct-controlled municipalities generated a rank correlation of 0.9665 across the remaining 26 provinces.
